{{Quote|Tython is beautiful and powerful, enigmatic and dangerous, filled with mysteries and open to those comfortable with the Force. It was here long, long before us, and these mysteries persisted with no eyes to see them, no minds to contemplate them. And that is why I fear Tython. It means everything to us, and yet we are nothing to it. We are merely passing through.|Je'daii recluse [[Ni'lander]]|<ref name="Into the Void" />}}
'''Tython''' was a [[Planet/Legends|planet]] in the [[Tython system/Legends|Tython system]] of the [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]] that played a pivotal role in the histories of the [[Je'daii Order]] and its successor, the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]]. A verdant world that was incredibly rich in [[The Force/Legends|the Force]], Tython was inhabited by an unknown [[Species/Legends|species]] hundreds of thousands of [[Standard year/Legends|years]] before the rise of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], and it was visited by both the [[Gree (species)/Legends|Gree]] and [[Kwa/Legends|Kwa]], two of the earliest species to have achieved interstellar travel. In [[36,453 BBY]], the great pyramid ships known as the [[Tho Yor]] brought pilgrims from over a dozen species from across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] to Tython, where the pilgrims learned to harness the Force and established the Je'daii Order, basing their philosophy of balance upon Tython's two [[Moon/Legends|moons]], [[Ashla (moon)/Legends|Ashla]] and [[Bogan]]. The Je'daii soon realized that Tython was unsafe for those who could not [[Force-sensitive/Legends|sense the Force]], and as a result, the [[Tythan]]s spread out to settle the other worlds of the Tython system.

In [[25,805 BBY]], after over ten thousand years of peace, Tython was the site of the final battle of the [[Despot War]], and [[25,793 BBY|twelve years later]], a [[Devourer (Rakatan ship)|vessel]] from the [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]] of the [[Rakata/Legends|Rakata]] species crashed on Tython's surface, sparking one of the intense [[Force Storm (Tython)|Force storms]] that occurred whenever the balance of Tython was shifted between the [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light]] and [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark sides of the Force]]. The [[Force Wars]] erupted not long afterwards, a devastating conflict fought between the followers of the light side and the followers of the dark side, and in the aftermath of the Force Wars, the victorious light-siders established the Jedi Order. The [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] departed Tython for the distant world of [[Ossus/Legends|Ossus]], leaving Tython to become lost as the Deep Core erased the [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlanes]] to the planet, and the savage [[Flesh Raider]]s evolved on the now-empty world.

==Description==
{{Quote|Never forget that we were brought here. Tython is a planet rich in the Force, but it is also a place of mystery, unknown to us, existing here for eons before the Tho Yor arrived. Its age is deep, its stories deeper.|Master Deela Jan Morolla|<ref name="Into the Void" />}}
[[File:Tython_forest.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Tython forest]] A terrestrial world in the [[Tython system/Legends|Tython system]] of the [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]], Tython was the fifth [[Planet/Legends|planet]] in orbit around the [[Star/Legends|star]] [[Tythos]],<ref name="Dawn of the Jedi 0" /> orbiting Tythos at a distance of less than 160 million kilometers, and the planet was incredibly rich with [[The Force/Legends|the Force]].<ref name="Into the Void" /> Tython possessed a breathable [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]] and a temperate climate, and it featured a number of continents separated by [[Ocean/Legends|oceans]] and seas. The planet was geographically varied, as Tython's continents were marked by plains, hills, mountains, and even canyons, and for much of the planet's history, Tython was a particularly verdant world. Tython was orbited by two [[Moon/Legends|moons]]: [[Ashla (moon)/Legends|Ashla]] and [[Bogan]], satellites that inspired the [[Je'daii Order]]'s philosophy of balance between the [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light]] and [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark sides of the Force]],<ref name="Dawn of the Jedi 0" /> and the Je'daii maintained sentry drones in orbits thirty thousand [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometers]] above Tython's surface.<ref name="Into the Void" /> Tython's environment was remarkably sensitive to the Force; powerful disturbances in the Force, such the presence of an individual particularly strong in either the light or dark side of the Force, could cause immense [[Force storm (weather)|Force storms]] and [[Groundquake/Legends|groundquakes]] that would ravage Tython's surface.<ref name="Dawn of the Jedi 0" /> However, by the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[990 BBY]], all hyperlanes to Tython had become [[Hyperspace collapse|unstable]] and forgotten, and the planet itself had been devastated—the planet was covered by a constant layer of storms, and its surface was the color of ash, with barren plains where immense forests had once stood.<ref name="Rule of Two" />

Tython was home to a large number of [[Species/Legends|species]] of creatures whose shapes and forms were as varied as the planet's surface, such as [[screech lizard]]s and [[acid spider]]s. Tython's [[hook hawk]]s were birds that possessed hooked beaks and sharp talons, and hunted their prey by hypnotizing them with song and then attacking. [[Silik lizard]]s were rare but deadly [[Silicon/Legends|silicon]]-based creatures that absorbed energy from sand itself. Six-limbed and the size of a [[Human/Legends|Human]] adult, silik lizards featured a large number of spikes on their bodies and were known to charge opponents on their hind legs. The [[Rift]] was home to many deadly creatures, many of which were unnamed and unknown. The [[saarl]] was a massive, purple worm with a tooth-filled maw that opened like a three-petaled flower. [[Flame tygah]]s were eight-limbed reptilian creatures twice the size of a Human that were native to Tython's [[Strafe Plains]]; a flame tygah's claws and tail dripped fire and its mouth blazed with heat. [[Blood spite/Legends|Blood spites]] were bat-like creatures that fed on warm blood and inhabited the [[Red Desert]], though their existence was widely considered to be only a rumor by the Je'daii. [[Ak tree/Legends|Ak trees]] were common in Tython's forests during the time of the Je'daii.<ref name="Into the Void" />

Tython's [[Moon Channel]] was home to the tentacled [[gelfish]] (have poisonous tentacles, could climb onto the sides of ships, attacked in flocks) as well as enormous sea serpents (have a head the size of a human torso, teeth that secrete poison).<ref name="Into the Void" /> The hoofed quadrupeds known as [[guid]]s were native to the region around [[Kaleth]],<ref name="Guid" /> the Je'daii Temple of Knowledge,<ref name="Dawn of the Jedi 0" /> and while they were not ordinarily aggressive, guids could attack their opponents with their powerful jaws and massive forelegs.<ref name="Guid" /> Like the guid, the mammalian [[Uxibeast/Legends|uxibeasts]] were also found in small groups on other worlds despite the fact that they were believed to have originated on Tython. Uxibeasts were ill-tempered herbivores that traveled in herds and were deceptively aggressive.<ref name="Uxibeast" /> The four-legged [[horranth]] were reptilian predators that hunted in large family groups and had enormous birth rates—their population was typically only constrained by a limited food supply.<ref name="Horranth" /> [[Manka cat/Legends|Manka cats]], feline predators from [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]], eventually found their way to Tython and thrived in the planet's vibrant ecosystem.<ref name="Manka" />

==History==
===Early history===
[[File:The_Old_City.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Old City.]]
Tens of thousands of years before [[36,453 BBY]], an unknown species constructed the [[Old City (Tython)|Old City]] on the continent of [[Talss]] on Tython. The [[Gree (species)/Legends|Gree]], one of the earliest species to achieve interstellar travel, visited Tython early in galactic history, though the Old City was long abandoned even by that time. The Gree inhabited the Old City for a time, and there were rumors that the Gree constructed a [[hypergate]]—a technology used by the Gree to travel instantaneously between two points in space—in the depths of the Old City. [[Lanoree Brock]] speculated that the city could have been built for giants.<ref name="Into the Void" />

The Gree eventually left Tython,<ref name="Into the Void" /> and the next species to visit the planet was the [[Kwa/Legends|Kwa]]. The Kwa linked Tython with their other worlds with an [[Infinity Gate]], a technology similar to a hypergate, but thousands of years before the rise of the Je'daii Order, the Kwa's encounter with the [[Rakata/Legends|Rakata]] species led them to destroy all remaining Infinity Gates in order to prevent the Rakata from overrunning the galaxy. The few remaining Kwa on Tython eventually died out after destroying their Infinity Gate.<ref name="Dawn of the Jedi 9">[[Dawn of the Jedi: The Prisoner of Bogan 4|''Dawn of the Jedi: The Prisoner of Bogan'' 4]]</ref>

===Je'daii Order===
{{Quote|The planet heralded their arrival with great storms. On this world, the travelers felt the energy that surrounded them. The same, mystical, primal energy—the same Force—that had first called them to the Tho Yor. On that day, the travelers became as one in the Force. The Tho Yor left the central pyramid to take the travelers to their new homes on this strange world. One in the Force, these travelers from diverse and distant worlds also became one people. They became Tythans.|Ketu|<ref name="Dawn of the Jedi 1" />}}
In the year 36,453 BBY, the eight great pyramid ships known as the [[Tho Yor]] [[Tho Yor Arrival|arrived]] at Tython, delivering [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] pilgrims from over a dozen worlds to the planet and causing an intense Force storm. The eight smaller ships met with the ninth and largest Tho Yor above a great pillar of stone that reached high into the sky on Tython, and then each of the eight departed in a different direction to a different location across Tython. The Tho Yor remained at their final destinations after depositing their passengers, and the pilgrims soon developed into a cohesive culture of [[Tythan]]s, realizing that the purpose of their gathering was for them to study the Force and harness its powers. Inspired by Tython's twin moons, the bright Ashla and dark Bogan, the Tythans came to understand the dual nature of the Force's light and dark sides, and they also realized that Tython itself would react to imbalance in the Force with powerful quakes and Force storms.<ref name="Dawn of the Jedi 1" />

[[File:Jedi_Order_on_Tython_JMGD.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The Je'daii Order established on Tython]]
With this knowledge, the Tythans formed the Je'daii Order, naming themselves after the word for "mystic center" in the [[Dai Bendu language|language]] of the [[Talid/Legends|Talid]] species's [[Order of Dai Bendu]]. The Je'daii built [[Je'daii Temples|nine great temples]] at the sites of the nine Tho Yor, some of which remained floating in the sky while others had landed in the oceans or on mountainsides.<ref name="Dawn of the Jedi 1" /> [[Padawan Kesh]], the Je'daii Academy, had been constructed at one of the Tho Yor by the year [[36,019 BBY]], when [[Nordia Gral]] was serving as the Temple's first [[Je'daii Temple Master|Temple Master]]. By that [[Time/Legends|time]], the Je'daii had completed temples at the other eight Tho Yor, and they also developed the tradition of a [[Great Journey]], a two-year odyssey across Tython's surface to each of the nine temples that would be undertaken by [[Padawan/Legends|Padawans]] once they became [[Je'daii Journeyer]]s. For the first thousand years of the Je'daii's time on Tython, the planet was frequently wracked by intense Force storms, as the Je'daii had not yet learned how to restore balance to the planet and calm the storms through the Force.<ref name="Into the Void" />

The Je'daii also constructed cities across Tython's surface, though as the pilgrims' second millennium on Tython came to an end, it became evident that those who were not Force-sensitive could not survive on the planet. The destruction of the [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Aurum]] inspired a [[second migration]], where those Tythans who were not Je'daii departed Tython in [[Starship/Legends|starships]] and settled the other worlds of the nine-planet Tython system. Force-sensitives born on the other planets, the [[Settled Worlds]], were brought to Tython for training as Je'daii, and the Tython system's way of life continued for over ten thousand years. However, resentment of the Je'daii among the Settled Worlds eventually led to conflict. In [[25,805 BBY]], the [[Despot Queen]] [[Hadiya]] united the crime [[Baron/Legends|barons]] of her [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] [[Shikaakwa]] and conquered the rest of the Settled Worlds. She then turned her attention to Tython, and her [[Army/Legends|army]] invaded the planet in a [[Battle of Tython|final battle]]—a battle that saw the [[Death/Legends|death]] of millions of Hadiya's troops and thousands of Je'daii.<ref name="Dawn of the Jedi 1" /> Hadiya herself was slain by the Je'daii [[Daegen Lok]] at the gates of Kaleth, bringing the [[Despot War]] to an end.<ref name="Dawn of the Jedi 9" />

Peace was shattered, however, circa [[25,793 BBY]],<ref name="T18">{{TORweb|url=holonet/galactic-history|text=Galactic History: The Force War on Tython}}</ref> when a schism in the Order's belief system pitted those who favored the Ashla philosophy against those who adhered to the Bogan school of thought. Wielding [[Force-imbued sword/Legends|Force-imbued metal swords]], the Je'daii were pitted in a bloody civil war known as the [[Force Wars]].<ref name="Atlas" /> The Ashla philosophers called themselves the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] and were led by a [[Jedi High Council/Legends|High Council]] comprising the greatest of their number. One of the High Councilors, the great Master [[Rajivari]], was corrupted by the dark side of the Force and led a faction of dissidents in another savage attack against the Jedi he had helped to create. Rajivari's camp fortified itself at the Temple of Knowledge, called Kaleth by the Order. While the Bogan philosophers held off the Jedi for several weeks, Master Rajivari disappeared, leaving his disciples in disarray. Weakened and taking heavy casualties, Rajivari's followers were defeated and the Jedi Order ended the uprising.<ref name="TOR" />

===Abandonment===
Initially, the Jedi believed their power was limited to Tython only, though this was later proven otherwise<ref name="JvS">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref> when a proactive group left Tython to liberate other worlds, becoming the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]]<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> around [[25,783 BBY]].<ref name="T17">{{TORweb|url=holonet/galactic-history|text=Galactic History: The Jedi Order is Established}}</ref> In the wake of the Force Wars, the victorious Jedi Order abandoned Tython in favor of [[Ossus/Legends|Ossus]], a lush planet on the edge of the [[Tion Cluster/Legends|Tion Cluster]] deep in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]]. Despite the Order's departure, Tython was absorbed into the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and was held throughout the [[Indecta Era|Indecta]], [[Kymoodon Era|Kymoodon]], and [[Pius Dea Era|Pius Dea]] eras and beyond.<ref name="TEGTW" />

Following the destruction of the [[Cron Cluster/Legends|Cron Cluster]] and the ensuing [[Battle of Ossus (Great Sith War)|ruination]] of Ossus, the Jedi Order had relocated to Coruscant; records of Tython's existence survived to this point, and notation of [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] experiments on the planet were made in the [[Jedi Archives/Legends|Archives]] of the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]]. Terrific beasts called [[Terentatek/Legends|terentateks]], the product of [[Sith alchemy/Legends|alchemy]], were loosed on Tython and were deemed monstrous abominations that posed as an affront to the Force by the Jedi High Council. Charging members of the Order to hunt down the creatures and execute them with extreme prejudice, the High Council initiated the [[Great Hunt (Jedi)|Great Hunt]], allowing any who wished to join in the purge to participate. Among other worlds, Tython was [[Cleansing of Tython|cleansed]] in [[3994 BBY]], ridding the ancient Jedi homeworld of the terentatek threat.<ref name="SaL">{{Tales|23|Shadows and Light}}</ref>

===Rediscovery===
Soon after the Great Hunt ended, hyperlanes to the planet collapsed and the world was left abandoned for several centuries. Tython had not been forgotten, however;<ref name="Journal" /> a new [[Tython hyperspace route (Satele Shan)|hyperspace route]] into the Deep Core was paved<ref name="TORE" /> by Jedi Knight [[Satele Shan]] in the wake of the [[Sacking of Coruscant]] by the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|reconstituted Sith Empire]].<ref name="Journal" /> Leading [[Jedi scout]]s to reclaim the world, Shan reestablished a Jedi presence on the world, making Tython the Order's fortress world during the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]] between the Sith Empire and the Galactic Republic. In the same time period, a group of [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] [[Pilgrims]] landed on the world and established a small [[Kalikori village|settlement]] near to the Jedi headquarters. Constructing their [[Jedi Temple (Tython)/Legends|Temple]] near the ruins of Kaleth, the Jedi kept their distance from the illegal Twi'lek settlement despite pleas from the Matriarch to assist in warding off [[Flesh Raider]]s.<ref name="TOR" />

During their return to Tython, the Jedi Order dedicated years to studying the planet, unearthing the history of the ancient Masters who once lived there. Having been violently uprooted from Coruscant, the Jedi Council sought a new foundation to rebuild upon. In the records of the ancient Force Wars and the holographic teachings of the first Jedi elders, the Order rediscovered forgotten knowledge: manuals of ethics, language ciphers, and more. This newfound wisdom, rooted in the traditions, morals, and worldview of the ancient Jedi, has since been integrated into the teachings of the modern Order.<ref name="TORE" />

Given that the Jedi of old were more engaged in warfare, modern Jedi have been able to contextualize their current struggles by learning from the strategies of the Force Wars and the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]]. Moreover, ancient techniques for crafting Jedi weapons have influenced the construction of modern [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsabers]].<ref name="TORE" />

[[File:Jedi_Temple_Tython.png|thumb|left|230px|The Jedi Temple on Tython erected after the [[Treaty of Coruscant]]]]
During the Cold War, [[Darth Angral]] of the Sith Empire destroyed the Republic [[Agriworld/Legends|agricultural world]] of [[Uphrades]] to issue a challenge to the former Padawan of Master [[Orgus Din]]. This [[Hero of Tython|Knight]] had come to be a thorn in the side of the Empire on several different occasions and had finally drawn Angral's wrath upon Tython. The Knight and their own apprentice, [[Kira Carsen]], entered Angral's [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]] the [[Oppressor (Harrower-class)|''Oppressor'']] and confronted Angral after disabling it. During the confrontation, the [[Tenebrae|Sith Emperor]] possessed Carsen from afar and ordered Angral to finish off the Knight. Ultimately the Knight was able to defeat Angral while Carsen refused to be the Emperor's pawn and was able to shatter the mental link. The two Jedi were able to flee the ''Oppressor'' before it exploded, taking Angral's corpse with it. Upon their return to the surface of the planet, [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]] Satele Shan bestowed the title "Hero of Tython" on the Jedi Knight for services done for the Order.<ref name="TOR" />

Shortly after the Hero's defense of Tython, a [[Galactic War|new war]] began between the Republic and the Sith Empire. In [[3637 BBY]], the Sith [[Assault on Tython|assaulted]] Tython and held the Jedi Temple for a short time. The assault was planned by the [[Dark Council]] member [[Darth Arkous]] and his subordinate, [[Lana Beniko]]. However Arkous was secretly a member of the [[Order of Revan]], and the attack was merely a means for the Revanites to obtain Rakatan technology from the Jedi Archives. A [[Korriban Incursion|simultaneous attack]] on [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]] was perpetrated by Arkous's secret ally, [[Colonel/Legends|Colonel]] [[Rian Darok]].<ref name="TOR" />

Following the [[Eternal Empire]]'s [[Eternal Empire conquest|conquest]], Tython had become largely abandoned as a result of the Jedi Order scattering to the far edges of the galaxy, save for those serving in archival and research capacities. By [[3627 BBY]], the Republic formed [[Task Force Nova]] to reunite the Order, but chose not to resettle on Tython, deciding to instead settle a new homeworld to be closer to the people they sought to defend.<ref name="Star Wars: The Old Republic: Onslaught">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Onslaught]]''</ref>

===Return to obscurity===
However, sometime after the Galactic War, Tython's surface was severely devastated in a catastrophe, and the planet became saturated with dark-side energy. During the [[New Sith Wars]] between the Republic and various Sith factions, the [[Shi'ido]] Sith Lord [[Belia Darzu]] took control of Tython and built a [[Belia Darzu's fortress|large fortress]] on the planet. Darzu, who was skilled in the use of ''[[mechu-deru]]''—the ability to transform the flesh of living beings into metal machines—had conducted experiments within the fortress, developing the ability to create [[technobeast]]s in the year [[1250 BBY]]. Building an army of the technological horrors and recording her knowledge within [[Holocron of Belia Darzu|her holocron]], Darzu initiated the phase of the New Sith Wars known as the [[Sictis Wars]].<ref name="Droids">''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref> However, Darzu incurred the wrath of the [[Mecrosa Order]]<ref name="END">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/insideronline/88/indexp2.html|text=''Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties''|int=Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties}}</ref> in [[1230 BBY]], and the Mecrosa [[Assassin/Legends|assassins]] [[Assassination of Belia Darzu|killed]] Darzu on Tython.<ref name="Droids" />

[[File:Duel_on_Tython.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The duel between the Jedi and Sith in Belia Darzu's fortress.]]
By the year [[990 BBY]], during the [[Golden Age of the Old Republic]], Tython had been long abandoned, as the hyperlanes to the planet had been lost. However, the Sith aspirant [[Hetton]] discovered navigational data on Tython, and he passed the coordinates for a long-forgotten [[Tython hyperspace route (Hetton)|hyperspace route]] to [[Darth Zannah/Legends|Darth Zannah]], a [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] and the apprentice of [[Darth Bane/Legends|Darth Bane]]. Bane traveled to Tython in order to [[Mission to Tython|investigate]] Darzu's fortress so that he could further his knowledge of holocrons, while his apprentice infiltrated the Archives of the Jedi Temple on Coruscant in search of information on the [[orbalisk]] creatures that Bane had been infected with. Bane took his [[Infiltrator-series long-range fighter|''Infiltrator''-series long-range fighter]] [[Mystic (starfighter)|''Mystic'']] to Tython and approached Darzu's fortress, destroying the fortress's defenses when they attacked his fighter. Bane then entered the fortress to find an army of dormant technobeasts, and the creatures attacked him after he retrieved Darzu's holocron. Bane destroyed all of the technobeasts and spent the next few days in meditation, studying the holocron in order to build his own.<ref name="Rule of Two" />

However, Zannah was discovered on Coruscant, and she was forced to flee to Tython with her cousin [[Darovit]]. The two were pursued by Jedi Masters [[Valenthyne Farfalla]], [[Raskta Lsu]], and [[Worror Dowmat]], along with Jedi Knights [[Johun Othone]] and [[Sarro Xaj]], and the five Jedi engaged the two Sith in a [[Duel on Tython|duel]] within Darzu's fortress. The duel ended with a Sith victory, though Bane was severely injured and Zannah was forced to take her master and Darovit to the planet [[Ambria/Legends|Ambria]] for healing.<ref name="Rule of Two" /> In the years that followed, the Jedi Order established an [[Jedi academy (Tython)|academy]] on Tython's surface despite the strong dark-side presence, and the facility served as a place for deeper immersion in the Force similar to the [[Culu Memorial Center|academy]] on [[Alpheridies/Legends|Alpheridies]].<ref name="Jedi Path">[[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force (real-life book)|''The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force'']]</ref>

During the [[Separatist Crisis/Legends|Separatist Crisis]], as public opinion slowly turned against the Jedi, conspiracy theorists insisted that the Jedi had found Tython once again and set up a secret temple there. The conspiracies often accompanied rumors of vast Jedi treasure hordes hidden on the planet. Few gave the rumors much credibility, but they have served as fodder for anti-Jedi [[Holovid/Legends|holovid]] pundits and as a lure for [[Treasure hunting/Legends|treasure hunters]]. The Jedi Master [[Ilia Orpin/Legends|Ilia Orpin]], who became the [[Gatekeeper/Legends|gatekeeper]] of a [[Jedi holocron/Legends|Jedi holocron]], provided an extensive account of Jedi history through the "[[Revan Mythologies]]"—a series of fables and myths that recounted the Order's history. Some scholars considered Orpin's works to be derivatives of the [[Qel-Droma Epics/Legends|Qel-Droma Epics]], a similar set of mythical stories that spoke of the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]] and the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]]. Many of the Mythologies describe countless temples and ruins on Tython, including those connected to the ancient Je'daii and to the Jedi Order.<ref name="NoP">''[[Nexus of Power]]''</ref>

During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the sectors of the Galactic Republic were assigned one of twenty [[Oversector/Legends|oversectors]], and were the operating theaters of the [[Troop/Legends|troops]] fighting the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], and the Tython system was placed in [[Sector 5/Legends|Sector 5]].<ref name="TEGTW" /> After establishing the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]<ref name="ROTS">{{Film|III}}</ref> in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]],<ref name="NEC" /> [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] brought the [[Tarkin Doctrine/Legends|Tarkin Doctrine]] into effect, reorganizing the oversectors into political and military entities, giving each Imperial [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]] authority over an oversector.<ref name="Imperial Handbook">''[[Star Wars: Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]''</ref> Palpatine appointed [[Cinzero Gann]] to be Grand Moff of Sector 5.<ref name="Shield">''[[Shield of Lies]]''</ref>

By [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]], Tython's role in the history of the Jedi Order was forgotten and the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] [[Historical Council]] noted that some said that the Jedi Order began on Ossus,<ref name="TEC">[[The Essential Chronology (real-world book)|''The Essential Chronology'']]</ref> but by [[36 ABY]] they had learned about Tython's role in the history of the Jedi Order.<ref name="NEC" />

==Inhabitants==
{{Quote|Perhaps there is a madness in remaining on Tython while not strong in the Force. One would not submerge long beneath the surface of the sea if one did not possess gills. One would surface. One would escape. So to stay here, now… that way, insanity lies.|Unknown Tythan, c. 9,000 TYA|<ref name="Into the Void" />}}
Tython was originally home to a species of immense size, as the Old City was built for individuals more than three times the size of a Human, though that species was long vanished by the time the Gree arrived.<ref name="Into the Void" /> The Gree eventually departed Tython, and the Kwa species eventually came to Tython for some time before they died out on the planet after destroying Tython's Infinity Gate.<ref name="Dawn of the Jedi 9" /> The pilgrims brought to Tython by the Tho Yor were of great variety and of many different species from across the galaxy: they included Talids, Humans, [[Selkath/Legends|Selkath]], Twi'leks, [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith]], [[Cathar/Legends|Cathar]], [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiees]], [[Zabrak/Legends|Zabrak]], [[Noghri/Legends|Noghri]], [[Devaronian/Legends|Devaronians]],<ref name="Dawn of the Jedi 1" /> [[Sullust/Legends|Sullustans]], [[Mirialan/Legends|Mirialans]],<ref name="Dawn of the Jedi 2">[[Dawn of the Jedi: Force Storm 2|''Dawn of the Jedi: Force Storm'' 2]]</ref> [[Iktotchi/Legends|Iktotchi]],<ref name="Dawn of the Jedi 9" /> [[Krevaaki]], [[Miraluka/Legends|Miraluka]],<ref name="Into the Void" /> and the species that would be later known as [[Koorivar/Legends|Koorivar]].<ref name="Dawn of the Jedi 8">[[Dawn of the Jedi: The Prisoner of Bogan 3|''Dawn of the Jedi: The Prisoner of Bogan'' 3]]</ref> The Flesh Raider species evolved on Tython in the millennia after the departure of the Jedi, and they had developed a primitive and savage culture by the time of the Cold War.<ref name="TOR" />

==Locations==
During the era of the Je'daii, Tython had a number of cities and temples, and its surface was geographically varied. [[Mahara Kesh]], the Je'daii Temple of Healing, was located in Tython's [[Deep Ocean]].<ref name="Dawn of the Jedi 0" /> The island continent of [[Masara]] was covered by forests and verdant plains, and [[Bodhi]], the Je'daii Temple of the Arts, was situated near the [[Edge Forest]] on Masara's southern coast, while the continent was bordered by the [[Thyrian Ocean]] on its northern coast. The continent of Thyr lay eight hundred kilometers to the north across the Thyrian Ocean, and Thyr featured rocky plains and the [[Stark Forests]], forests with trees that sucked moisture from the air and stored it as water in large sacs on their branches. Thyr was also home to the [[Silent Desert]], a desert with the unique property that all sound was soaked up by an unknown quality in the desert's sands. The Silent Desert also featured intense winds and a number of sand sculptures that some believed to be [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]]. The Temple of Force Skills, [[Qigong Kesh]], was in an enormous cavern beneath the Silent Desert.<ref name="Into the Void" />

The continent of [[Kato Zakar]], which lay to the south of Thyr, was often called the Firelands in the Je'daii era for its tumultuous terrain and the significant amount of volcanic activity that was common in the continent's heartlands, almost thirty-two hundred kilometers south of the northern coast. The [[Ice Giant Range]], a mountain range that was the site of the Temple of Martial Arts [[Stav Kesh]], was located almost five hundred kilometers inland from the northern coast, and the Strafe Plains lay between the Ice Giants and the coast. The Strafe Plains were a cold, windswept scrubland that was prone to frequent Force storms and scattered with magma-filled "swallow holes" and columns of razor-sharp silica. Kato Zakar's eastern reaches were covered by fungi forests, then swamps, and then sand dunes the farther one got to the continent's eastern coast, and the port city of [[Ban Landing]] was located on Kato Zakar's coastline at the sea known as the Moon Channel.<ref name="Into the Void" />

Across the Moon Channel was Tython's largest continent, Talss, also known as the Dark Continent. Talss was marked by the massive canyon known as the Rift—a geographic feature which was the site of frequent volcanic and seismic activity. The two continents were separated by a distance of a hundred kilometers (three days of sailing), and the Moon Channel between them was the site of the seven [[Moon Islands]]. Talss's western coast was home to a number of small ports. Six hundred kilometers east of the Rift was a mountain range split by the [[Chasm]],<ref name="Into the Void" /> and [[Anil Kesh]], the Temple of Science, straddled the Chasm high in the mountains. and something within the Chasm's depths interfered with the senses of Force users.<ref name="Dawn of the Jedi 0" /> South of the Rift and the mountains lay a wide, seemingly endless plain that lacked any plant growth over waist height, as the plain's intense wind stripped any plants that grew taller from the soil. To the south of the plains, in the southern reaches of Talss, was the Red Desert. The Old City was about eighty kilometers inward from the northern edges of the desert, half buried in the sands by the time of the Je'daii.<ref name="Into the Void" />

[[Vur Tepe]], the Je'daii Forge, was situated directly over an active volcano in a mountain range during the era of the Je'daii, while [[Akar Kesh]], the Temple of Balance, was situated at a towering pillar of stone—the site of the original landing of the Tho Yor.<ref name="Dawn of the Jedi 0" /> Six waterfalls cascaded from the top of the monolith, feeding into the series of lakes and rivers around the pillar's base.<ref name="Dawn of the Jedi 6">[[Dawn of the Jedi: The Prisoner of Bogan 1|''Dawn of the Jedi: The Prisoner of Bogan'' 1]]</ref> Kaleth, the Je'daii Temple of Knowledge, was built over a [[Vergence/Legends|Force nexus]] near the river and mountain range that would be known by the Jedi tens of thousands years later as the [[Tythos River]] and the [[Tythos Ridge]].<ref name="TOR" />

Following the Jedi Order's resettlement of the planet, a massive Temple was erected near the site of the ruined city-temple of Kaleth. The Temple served as a base for all Jedi operations on the planet for several years; the Jedi also occupied a structure known as the [[Masters' Retreat]] located in the [[Tythonian Gnarls]], while the Twi'lek Kalikori village was on a ridge just above the Temple complex.<ref name="TOR" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Tython_waterfalls.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Concept art of Tython]]
{{Quote|Luke, you don't even know the 'grip of tython' or 'the seven moves.' You can't…|Leia Lars|<ref name="Second Draft">''[[Adventures of the Starkiller, Episode I: The Star Wars]]''</ref>}}
The term "tython" originates in the [[Adventures of the Starkiller, Episode I: The Star Wars|second draft]] of what would become [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']].<ref name="Second Draft" /> Tython was first mentioned in the [[2002]] sourcebook ''[[Power of the Jedi Sourcebook]]'', where it's identified as a planet that is a possible location of the discovery of the Force.<ref name="POTJ">''[[Power of the Jedi Sourcebook]]''</ref> ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' identified Tython as the planet that was believed to be the birthplace of the Jedi Order.<ref name="NEC" /> This was confirmed in the supplementary material preceding the [[2011]] release of the [[Star Wars video games|massively multiplayer online role-playing game]] ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'',<ref name="Holonet" /> in which the planet plays a prominent role in the early gaming experience for players who chose the path of the [[Jedi Consular]] or Jedi Knight.<ref name="TOR" />
